THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT In this appeal, the injured petitioner is seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T., Kundapura ('the Tribunal' in short) by order dated 16.08.2016 in M.V.C.No.182/2015.
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are, the petitioner has sustained injuries on his head and left leg and other grievous injuries in an accident that occurred on 02.11.2014 at about 02:00 am while travelling in a lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-20/B-5648 near Bidkalkatte College, Hardalli-Mandalli Village of Kundapura Taluk.
After taking the treatment, he has approached the Tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.8,90,000/-.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance NC: 2023:KHC:29524 Company.
The Tribunal after taking the evidence, passed the impugned judgment awarding Rs.1,14,670/- with interest of 6% p.a.
Pleading inadequacy, seeking enhancement of the compensation, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri. Nagaraja Hegde, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. B.C.
Shivannegowda, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that in spite of the petitioner suffered fracture of left tibia and diffuse cerebral edema, the Tribunal has not considered the gravity of the injuries sustained and the notional income is taken on the lower side at Rs.7,000/- as against Rs.8,500/- being taken in the Lok Adalat and sought for enhancement of compensation.
NC: 2023:KHC:29524 6.
Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that in the year 2014, for a person with no proof of income, it has to be assessed at Rs.8,500/-.
Keeping that in mind, a nominal enhancement has to be made.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed and also perused the materials on record.
8. The materials on record undisputedly point out the accident, injuries sustained by the petitioner and his entitlement to claim the compensation.

No doubt, the petitioner is entitled to claim just Mohammad Shafiq vs Rajesh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114898917/
2 compensation and it shall neither be inadequate nor a bonanza.

sentences.text: The medical records point out that the petitioner has suffered head injury with diffuse cerebral edema and fracture of left tibia.

He has also spent money towards treatment, but the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering, medical expenses, loss of earning NC: 2023:KHC:29524 during laid-up period and loss of amenities and discomfort needs little enhancement.

Hence, a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards pain and suffering, a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomfort, a sum of Rs.6,000/- towards loss of income during laid-up period and Rs.4,000/- towards medical expenses could be the enhancement that the petitioner is entitled in the facts and circumstances of the case,
having regard to the nature of evidence let in before the Tribunal.
In all, a sum of Rs.40,000/- global enhancement will compensate the petitioner in addition to a sum of Rs.1,14,670/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appeal merits consideration, in result, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The impugned judgment is modified.
NC: 2023:KHC:29524 iii) The petitioner is entitled to an enhanced global compensation of Rs.40,000/- with interest of 6%

p.a.
iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
v) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal.
